skill.name: revnu-get-listed
skill.description: Get onto the third-party pages AI answers and search cite when buyers ask for the best tool in your category: "best X" roundups, directories, review sites, GitHub awesome lists, community threads and comparison pages. Finds which ones are cited, ranks them by fit and effort, and drafts each submission, PR or pitch by the target's own rules. Use when the user says "get us listed", "which directories should we submit to", "how do we get into best-of lists", "why does ChatGPT recommend competitors and not us", "get mentioned in AI answers", "submit to awesome lists", "get on G2", "where are our competitors listed", "pitch listicle authors", "find backlink opportunities", "launch directories", "get into roundups", "Product Hunt alternatives", "where should we be listed", "get cited by Perplexity". Never submits, pays or posts without a yes. Works without a Revnu account.
skill.summary: Find relevant third-party listing opportunities, rank them by evidence and effort, and draft submissions using each target's rules.
skill.author: revnu-app

security_audit.summary: All 46 static findings are false positives involving Markdown, policy language, or legitimate tools and consent-gated requests. No evidence found of malicious shell execution, system reconnaissance, or secret exfiltration. One semantic consent risk remains: the connected Revnu handoff can delegate ongoing submissions without explicitly requiring approval before delegation.

remediation.issue: The connected Revnu handoff lacks an explicit consent gate and delegates submissions under service-controlled approval settings.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval before sending the brief; preview its contents and require separate target-specific approval before every delegated submission.

semantic_findings.title: Connected Service Delegation Lacks Explicit Consent
semantic_findings.description: The connected branch says to offer a handoff, then call ask_revnu with business context and instructions to submit suitable free listings. It does not explicitly wait for acceptance, and delegates approval to service settings rather than preserving target-specific consent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The handoff explicitly transmits a brief and requests ongoing submissions without an acceptance step. General target-specific consent rules reduce certainty about execution but conflict with service-controlled approvals.

content.user_title: Find Listing Opportunities and Draft Submissions
content.value_statement: Buyers may find competitors on third-party pages while your product remains absent. This skill researches relevant pages, ranks opportunities, and drafts submissions using each publisher's rules.
actual_capabilities: Develops 8-15 buyer questions from product context and competitor information.
Collects candidate pages from supplied citations, available engine APIs, web search, and competitor listings.
Checks submission rules, eligibility, activity, existing competitors, and listing costs.
Ranks opportunities by evidence, audience fit, effort, and cost without inventing numeric scores.
Drafts directory fields, awesome-list entries, editorial pitches, review-profile text, and disclosed community replies.
Produces a research receipt and can save a listings tracker after permission.
limitations: Listings do not guarantee acceptance, AI citations, traffic, or search rankings.
Research coverage depends on accessible pages, host search tools, supplied citations, and available API credentials.
Search results are proxies, not proof of citations in consumer AI answers.
Ongoing Revnu monitoring is optional and paid; its connected handoff needs careful consent review.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Product Launch
use_cases.description: Identify relevant directories and review sites, confirm eligibility, and prepare field-by-field submissions before launch.

use_cases.title: Research Missing AI Mentions
use_cases.description: Compare competitor appearances across buyer questions and prioritize third-party pages with documented citation evidence.

use_cases.title: Prepare Curated-List Contributions
use_cases.description: Check awesome-list requirements and prepare compliant entry text and pull request drafts for eligible developer tools.

prompt_templates.title: Find Initial Opportunities
prompt_templates.prompt: Read our README and public website. Identify relevant free listing opportunities and explain the evidence for each. Do not submit anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner research for a product without an existing listing plan.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Competitor Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [category] for [buyer segment], using [competitors]. Rank candidate pages by evidence, fit, effort, and cost. Distinguish real citations from search proxies.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Target-Specific Drafts
prompt_templates.prompt: Check these targets: [URLs]. Read each submission policy and verify eligibility. Draft compliant submissions for eligible targets; mark missing facts. Do not post.
prompt_templates.scenario: Detailed drafting for a selected shortlist.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Evidence-Based Listing Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use our growth context and [citation report] to prioritize ten targets. Prepare five compliant drafts and a research receipt. Ask before saving a tracker. Do not contact Revnu or submit anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning with existing citation evidence and local context.

output_examples.input: Prepare free listing opportunities for a developer tool. No verified citation report is available.
output: Evidence: Host search only; these results do not prove AI citations.
First priority: An active curated list with relevant competitors, matching eligibility, and a one-line submission format.
Not now: A review site that excludes beta products.
Receipt: Rules and eligibility checked; nothing submitted.

output_examples.input: Prepare directory text for an uptime-monitoring tool. Its confirmed features are HTTP checks and email alerts.
output: Short description: Monitor HTTP endpoints and receive email alerts.
Status: Draft only. Confirm the target's category, field limits, and eligibility before submission.

best_practices: Provide current product facts, competitor names, and citation reports when available.
Check each target's current rules and preserve source links for factual claims.
Approve each submission separately and explicitly review any external service handoff.
anti_patterns: Treating search appearances as proof of AI citations or guaranteed traffic.
Submitting generic promotional text without checking eligibility and publisher rules.
Using fake reviews, undisclosed affiliations, purchased ranking links, or unauthorized bulk submissions.

faq.question: Do I need a Revnu account?
faq.answer: No. Research and drafting work without an account. Revnu offers optional paid monitoring and listing support.

faq.question: Does the skill submit listings automatically?
faq.answer: The main workflow requires approval for each target. The connected Revnu handoff has a consent ambiguity identified in this audit.

faq.question: Can it work without AI engine API keys?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use supplied citation reports and host web search. Search-only results must be labeled as proxies.

faq.question: Which kinds of pages can it research?
faq.answer: It covers roundups, directories, review sites, GitHub awesome lists, community threads, and third-party comparison pages.

faq.question: Will a listing guarantee AI recommendations?
faq.answer: No. Acceptance, citations, traffic, and rankings are not guaranteed. Evidence must be checked for your category.

faq.question: How does it handle restrictive submission policies?
faq.answer: It checks eligibility and format requirements. Ineligible targets are deferred; AI-writing restrictions are disclosed for the user to handle.
